- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and overshoot; reduce forecast slope slightly.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downside.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overreacts and continues upward; cap forecast growth to 3–5% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.25), model often drifts toward mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted downward 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to pivot; force a 1–2 day lagged correction in forecast direction.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation; introduce exponential decay weighting toward recent 7-day average to reduce overfitting to recent spikes.
